description: NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter: 3D multibond airframe, coaxial BEMT rotors fitted to the JPL hover test, flight control after Grip et al. 2018. Reference values: published flight and test data (design/validation_data.json, design/jpl_hover_test.json) and the independent numpy BEMT trim of design/rotor_ref.py. Generated by design/build_model.py.

published Flight One hover rotor power 'about 210 W' (NASA21, design/validation_data.json); model 208 W. Tolerance 10 %: the published figure is rounded and the 78 % drive efficiency (Kon18) is one number for all loads

published Flight One upper collective 8.2 deg (NASA21); model 8.60 deg. JPL's own pre-flight model predicted 9.0 deg, 0.8 deg above the flight value; the model sits between the two. Tolerance 0.8 deg, the size of that published model error
published Flight One lower collective 9.2 deg (NASA21); model 9.86 deg (JPL pre-flight prediction 9.9 deg)
published hover altitude 3 m
published altitude hold 'within about 1 cm' (NASA21); the model's navigation is perfect, so it meets this bound easily
the planned 96 deg turn, held within the published 1.5 deg
published horizontal position variations of about 25 cm in the gusty wind (NASA21): a bound only; the model flies a steady wind with perfect navigation

published: cyclic 'generally below 3 deg' in 4-6 m/s winds (NASA21). The model needs 3.3 deg in a steady 5 m/s wind (Pitt-Peters edgewise moment x 2.5, Grip17), slightly above the published figure; bound 3.5 deg
